interest: Shows 1941 police pressure on American President Lines in Kobe via a staged employee strike, amid harassment of Western firms.
overview: Despatch No. 181 (July 1941): Consul Warner reports a July 3-10 strike by American President Lines employees in Kobe demanding retirement allowances and bonuses; Agent McCaskey refused all demands, and workers returned without concessions, amid Japanese police pressure implying he could not leave Kobe without a settlement.

people.name: S. F. McCaskey
people.role: Acting General Agent of the American President Lines at Kobe

people.name: J. M. Conway
people.role: Passenger Agent of the American President Lines at Kobe

subfiles.about: Report on a strike of Japanese employees at the American President Lines office in Kobe and subsequent Japanese police intimidation and involvement.
subfiles.from: Gerald Warner, American Consul at Kobe, Japan
subfiles.summary: Consul Warner reports a July 3-10, 1941 strike by American President Lines employees in Kobe over retirement allowances and bonuses after a dismissal; Agent McCaskey rejected all demands, and workers returned without concessions, while Japanese police interrogated McCaskey and implied he could not leave Kobe unsettled, suggesting police instigation.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 181 from American Consul Gerald Warner on Strike of Japanese Employees of American President Lines at Kobe
